\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{недавно} (nedávno)}{недавно (nedávno)}]{\ru{недавно} (nedávno) — recently}

\label{lesson:RU-C137-nedavno}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for (to) nowhere, then the Russian for what for.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{недавно}}
\textbf{\ru{недавно}} (\emph{nedávno}) — \textquotedblleft{}recently\textquotedblright{}. Russian's past usually ends in \textbf{-\ru{л}}, with \textbf{-\ru{ла}} for a woman: \textbf{\ru{Недавно} \ru{я} \ru{читал} \ru{книгу}.} — \emph{nedávno ya chitál knígu} — \textquotedblleft{}Recently I read a book.\textquotedblright{} A woman says \textbf{\ru{читала}}.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{прошлый} (próshlyy)}{прошлый (próshlyy)}]{\ru{прошлый} (próshlyy) — last, past}

Before the new one: say the Russian for long ago; for a long time, then the Russian for before.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{прошлый}}
\textbf{\ru{прошлый}} (\emph{próshlyy}) — \textquotedblleft{}last, past\textquotedblright{}.
